definition: A model specifically trained to convert text (or other data) into dense vector representations optimized for tasks like similarity search or clustering.
details: Embedding models are a distinct category from generative LLMs, optimized for producing representations useful for downstream retrieval and comparison tasks rather than for generating fluent text.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Embedding Model.
